original_value: Steganography is used for secret or covert communication. A graph wavelet transform‐based steganography using graph signal processing (GSP) is presented, which results in better visual quality stego image as well as extracted secret image. In the proposed scheme, graph wavelet transforms of both the cover image and transformed secret image (using Arnold cat map) are taken followed by alpha blending operation. The GSP‐based inverse wavelet transform is performed on the resulting image, to get the stego image. Here, the use of GSP increases the inter‐pixel correlation that results in better visual quality stego and extracted secret image as shown in simulation results. Simulation results show that the proposed scheme is more robust than other existing steganography techniques.

result.paraphrase: Steganography is used for covert or secret communication. This work presents a graph signal processing (GSP) steganography scheme based on graph wavelet transforms, producing better visual quality in both the stego image and the extracted secret image. In the proposed method, graph wavelet transforms are applied to the cover image and to the secret image after Arnold cat map transformation, followed by alpha blending. The resulting image is then processed with the GSP-based inverse wavelet transform to obtain the stego image. By increasing inter-pixel correlation, GSP improves the visual quality of both the stego and extracted secret images, as simulation results show. The simulations also indicate that the proposed scheme is more robust than other existing steganography techniques.
